preamble: Fronting of a velar stop all the way to a palatalized dental [tʲ] is a rare outcome of velar palatalization; most languages stop at [c] or continue to [tʃ]. It is a defining innovation of the Southern New England Algonquian languages: in Massachusett (Wampanoag) /k/ became the new phoneme /tʲ/ before Proto-Eastern Algonquian *eː (Massachusett /aː/), *əw, and a weakened *iː, giving wetu /wiːtʲəw/ 'house' beside the velar of Abenakian and Unami wigwam, weekuwôm. Quiripi took the same palatalization further to /tʃ/, and /k/ was often restored by analogy before /aː/ and /əw/.

examples.note: The velar became /tʲ/ (spelled ⟨ty⟩ in the modern orthography) before /əw/; the cognate wigwam (Abenakian/Unami) keeps k.

sources: Oxford, W. (2023). Consonant inventories from Proto-Algonquian to the daughter languages. https://home.cc.umanitoba.ca/~oxfordwr/algling/consonantchanges.html
